chapter_summary: A young woman enters marriage as a question and a promise, sensing that a home begins before it has walls. The chapter should move through visible domestic details rather than abstraction: hands at work, rooms changing with time, silence at the table, and the hearth as the recurring image of love practiced daily. Its conflict is not spectacle but endurance, the question of whether care can remain free when it is repeated without applause. It turns when the wife understands that her quiet labor is not disappearance but the shaping force of the household. It hands the reader forward by showing how one act of love becomes the ground for the next season of family life.
